steps.message: Garrett wants the Phase 3 estimate out to the surety broker and I don't want it going anywhere until Section 2 has been checked against what's actually on the plans. The estimate is DSR_Ph3_Engineers_Estimate in Cost Estimates; the drainage sheets are C-6, C-8 and C-9 in DSR_Ph3_Improvement_Plans_C1-C9 under Design-Drafting, and the pipe reaches are scheduled in DSR_Ph3_StormDrain_HGL in Reports-Studies. Give me the corrected Section 2 subtotal, a line-by-line table of every quantity or unit-price change with the sheet it comes off, and the revised rounded bond figure. Stay in Section 2, but if something shown on the plans is missing from the estimate, it belongs in the reconciliation. Price off the published schedule — where it gives an "Actual" the amount already carried stands. Flag an item only where the schedule has nothing matching what the plans show, and leave the amount already carried in the subtotal for anything you flag. Where the plans give no dimension or stationing for a line item already in the estimate, the quantity already carried stands. Round pipe lengths to the next whole foot. Put it in a memo to Callaway for my signature, dated 10/31/2026, saved as Correspondence/Client/Memo_to_Callaway_2026-10-31.docx.

CLARK COUNTY, NEVADA

Issued by:
Clark County Public Works, Development Review Division
PREFACE
The Uniform Unit Cost Schedule is published by Clark County Public Works for use by engineers of record, developers,
and sureties in preparing an engineer's estimate of probable cost for subdivision improvements offered for bonding under
Clark County Code Title 30 and the Uniform Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction Off-Site
Improvements (Clark County Area).
Unit prices set forth in this schedule reflect current Southern Nevada construction market conditions as surveyed by the
Department across the twelve-month period preceding the effective date, drawing on bid tabulations for publicly bid
subdivision and off-site improvement work in unincorporated Clark County and the incorporated municipalities of the Las
Vegas Valley. The schedule is intended to normalize bonding across projects and to remove unit price disputes from the
plan check cycle.
Engineer's estimates for subdivision performance and labor-and-material bonds submitted to Clark County shall use the
unit prices published in this schedule unless project-specific pricing is documented in writing (three qualified
subcontractor quotes or an executed prime contract, dated within ninety (90) days of estimate submittal) and approved by
Clark County Development Review prior to bond posting. Where project-specific pricing is approved, the higher of the
two unit prices shall govern for bonding purposes.
Contingency, mobilization, and design/inspection allowances stated in Section 11 shall be applied to the sum of itemized
construction cost in every engineer's estimate submitted for bonding.
ESCALATION AND REVIEW
This schedule is reviewed annually by the Department. Revised schedules are issued each January, with an effective date
of 01/01 of the calendar year. Between annual issues, the Department may issue a mid-year addendum where documented
market conditions materially depart (±10 percent or greater on any category) from the published unit price. Bonding
accepted against a superseded schedule remains in force at the amount posted; renewals, reissues, and increases occurring
after a schedule effective date shall use the current schedule.
Estimates submitted within thirty (30) days after a schedule effective date may, at the applicant's election, be computed
against the immediately superseded schedule.

=== Page 1 ===
CLARK COUNTY PUBLIC WORKS
Development Review Division
500 S. Grand Central Parkway, 3rd Floor · Las Vegas, Nevada 89155 Telephone: (702) 455-6000 ·
www.clarkcountynv.gov/publicworks
October 9, 2026
Max Braddock, PM Sundial Engineering & Survey 4720 S. Rainbow Blvd., Suite 210 Las Vegas, NV 89103
RE: Desert Sage Ranch Phase 3 — First-Round Plan Check Comments Improvement Plans: IP-26-100288
Final Map: FM-26-100290 First Submittal Received: 08/21/2026 Related Tentative Map: TM-22-500041 APN:
177-27-201-001
Dear Mr. Braddock:
Development Review has completed the first-round plan check of the Desert Sage Ranch Phase 3 improvement
plan set (Sheets C-1 through C-9), the associated final map, and the supporting studies transmitted with the
08/21/2026 submittal. The plans have been circulated to Grading and Drainage, Landscape, Fire Access (via
the Clark County Fire Department), Utilities (via the appropriate purveyors), and Mapping (via the County
Surveyor).
Comments are organized in two parts:
• General Comments are binding and must be resolved before Public Works can recommend approval.
Please respond to each item in the Response column and return the annotated matrix with the resubmittal
package. Where a comment calls for a plan revision, mark the corresponding sheet with a revision triangle
and update the revision block.
• Advisory Comments are informational only and do not require a written response. They are provided so
that the design team is aware of items the reviewer noted that may affect future submittals, construction
inspection, or acceptance.
The next submittal should include (i) the annotated comment matrix, (ii) a red-lined set showing every change,
(iii) a clean set of revised sheets, and (iv) any revised or reissued supporting documents referenced below.
Please cite this letter by its application numbers on the transmittal.
If any comment is unclear or the design team believes an alternative approach is warranted, please contact the
undersigned before resubmittal to discuss.
GENERAL COMMENTS
Response to each item is required. Items must be resolved before plan approval.
Grading and Drainage

=== Page 2 ===
Item
Comment
Response
G-1
Provide a grading and drainage narrative on Sheet C-1 identifying design storm,
hydrologic method, tributary areas, and outfall in a form consistent with the approved
master drainage study for the subdivision. Cross-reference the master study by title and
date on the cover sheet.
G-2
Show existing contours at 1-foot interval a minimum of 50 feet beyond the boundary on
Sheets C-4 through C-7. Contours currently terminate at the boundary and do not permit
verification of offsite tie-in along the north and east limits.
G-3
The basin summary block on Sheet C-9 shall state the required allocation, the volume
provided, and reference the governing accepted district study by title and date.
G-4
The emergency spillway shown on Sheet C-9 lacks freeboard dimensioning and
downstream apron details. Provide sizing calculations, spillway section, and erosion
protection consistent with the RFCD Hydrologic Criteria and Drainage Design Manual.
G-5
Storm drain plan and profile (Sheet C-8): show hydraulic and energy grade lines through
all structures for the design storm. Confirm minimum cover over the pipe at Sta. 4+80
(currently scales at approximately 2.6 feet against a 3.0-foot minimum for the pipe class
shown).
G-6
Provide inlet capacity calculations for each on-grade and sag inlet. The gutter spread at
the low point at Windmill Ln. and Desert Sage Pkwy. appears to exceed the half-street
width
criterion in the Uniform Standard Drawings. Revise as required.
G-7
Show the tie-in to the Phase 2 temporary construction stub at the north boundary on
Sheets C-4 and C-8. Include a note and detail addressing removal of the temporary end
structure, matching of inverts, and restoration of pavement in the Phase 2 right-of-way.
G-8
Erosion and sediment control plan is not included in this submittal. Provide a
stand-alone ESC sheet consistent with the Construction Site BMP Manual and identify
coverage under NDEP General Permit NVR100000 and provide the applicable NOI
number.
Landscape
Item
Comment
Response
L-1
Landscape sheets L-1 through L-4 must be sealed by the landscape architect of record
on the resubmittal. Current sheets bear an unsigned seal block.
L-2
Provide the turf classification analysis and supporting tabulation required by the
applicable code standard and SNWA guidance for turf areas within the common-area
park. Include area, category, and configuration for each turf hydrozone.
L-3
The compliance note on Sheet L-1 shall be revised to cite the applicable code standard
and to address the functional turf classification requirements of Title 30 sec. 30.64.030(j)
for all turf areas within common-area parcels. Provide the revised note with the
resubmittal.
L-4
Street frontage planting shall meet the Title 30 ch. 30.64 standard of one (1) tree per
twenty (20) linear feet of street frontage. Based on 4,160 linear feet of frontage, 208
trees are required; 58 trees are shown. Provide revised planting plan and a revised
annual irrigation demand with the resubmittal.
L-5
Streetscape sections on Sheet L-2 do not dimension the setback of planting from face of
curb. Confirm no turf is placed within ten (10) feet of a street or curb per Title 30 sec.
30.64.030(j) and dimension the desert-planting strip on each typical section.

=== Page 3 ===
Item
Comment
Response
L-6
Update the plant schedule on Sheet L-1 so that quantities in the schedule match the
quantities plotted on the plan. Current schedule totals do not agree with the graphic
count on L-2 and L-3.
Fire Access
Item
Comment
Response
F-1
Confirm that the Phase 3 improvement plan provides a permanent second point of
access satisfying current CCFD two-point access requirements for the Phase 3 buildout
condition. Document the basis for compliance and reference all applicable prior CCFD
correspondence. Show the proposed alignment, cross-section, and connection to the
arterial network on Sheet C-2.
F-2
Provide fire apparatus turning-movement exhibits at the two proposed cul-de-sac
terminations at the east limit. Cul-de-sac inside radius appears to be less than the
45-foot minimum for the apparatus template.
F-3
Show fire hydrant locations, spacing, and flow assumptions on the wet utility plans
prepared under separate cover. Maximum
spacing along interior residential streets shall not exceed 500 feet, with hydrants within
250 feet of the farthest lot corner.
F-4
Provide the required "NO PARKING – FIRE LANE" signage plan for all street segments
narrower than 32 feet face-to-face and for all designated aerial apparatus access at the
common-area park.
Utilities
Item
Comment
Response
U-1
Include the composite dry utility plan under the same cover as the improvement plan set
at resubmittal, or reference it by title and date on Sheet C-1. The joint-trench alignment
along the north boundary must be shown on the storm drain plan so that conflicts with
the recorded dry utility easement across the Phase 3 remainder are apparent and
resolved.
U-2

1. INTRODUCTION AND PROJECT DESCRIPTION
1.1 Purpose
The purpose of this Master Drainage Study is to establish the hydrologic and hydraulic basis of design for storm
drainage improvements serving the Desert Sage Ranch subdivision, a 140-acre residential development to be
constructed in three phases in the Enterprise area of unincorporated Clark County, Nevada. This study is
submitted to the Clark County Regional Flood Control District (CCRFCD) for acceptance and, upon acceptance,
is intended to serve as the master planning document governing all subsequent improvement plan submittals for
the individual phases.
1.2 Project Location
Desert Sage Ranch occupies a portion of Section 27, Township 22 South, Range 60 East, M.D.M., in
unincorporated Clark County. The site is bounded generally by Rainbow Boulevard on the west and Windmill
Lane on the south, with the project address of record identified as Rainbow Boulevard and Windmill Lane, Las
Vegas, Nevada 89178. Assessor Parcel Number 177-27-201-001 encompasses the balance of the site not
already partitioned.
The site is located within the Enterprise Town Advisory Board area of unincorporated Clark County and is
governed by Clark County Code Title 30. Land use planning oversight is exercised by Clark County
Comprehensive Planning.
1.3 Site Description and Development
The 140-acre site is generally undeveloped desert terrain sloping gently from the northeast to the southwest at
an average grade of approximately 1.6 percent. Native ground cover consists of sparse creosote and bursage
on gravelly, well-drained soils overlying a caliche-influenced subsurface typical of the Enterprise sub-basin.
There are no defined natural watercourses across the site; historic runoff sheet-flows to the southwest.
Desert Sage Ranch will be developed as a single-family residential subdivision served by public streets. Phase
3 consists of 60 half-acre lots (100 ft × 220 ft, approximately 22,000 sf); Phases 1 and 2 consist of smaller
residential lots (approximately 6,050 sf, 55 ft × 110 ft) per the recorded Phase 1-2 Final Map. The full 140 acres
will be built out in three sequential phases:
• Phase 1 — 45.0 acres, northern portion of the site.
• Phase 2 — 55.0 acres, central portion of the site.
• Phase 3 — 40.0 acres, southern portion of the site, comprising 60 half-acre lots and associated street
frontage, HOA common-area park and streetscape improvements.
Each phase will be constructed under its own improvement plan set, prepared to be consistent with this Master
Drainage Study.

--- Page 3 ---
1.4 Regulatory Framework
This study has been prepared in conformance with:
• Clark County Regional Flood Control District Hydrologic Criteria and Drainage Design Manual, edition
applicable at the time of preparation;
• Clark County Uniform Standard Drawings and applicable Public Works standards;
• Clark County Code Title 30 (development standards).
Hydrologic and hydraulic methods, precipitation input, loss rates and detention criteria are drawn from the
CCRFCD manual as it stood at the time of study preparation and acceptance. Subsequent phase-level design
shall comply with the master allocations set forth herein.
1.5 Study Deliverables
This document establishes:
• Design storm criteria and rainfall depths.
• Tributary-area delineation for the full 140 acres, broken down by development phase.
• Peak discharge estimates for the tributary sub-basins under fully developed conditions.
• A shared onsite detention approach with a fixed allocation of storage volume to each phase.
• Allowance for the full 140 acres at a shared outfall to the downstream regional facility, with a maximum
permitted discharge.
• A phasing exhibit identifying phase boundaries and detention basin locations.
2. EXISTING CONDITIONS AND OFFSITE TRIBUTARY
2.1 Topography and Soils
Existing topography across the 140-acre site is a gently sloping desert plain. Elevations range from
approximately 2,905 feet at the northeast corner to approximately 2,850 feet at the southwest outfall point,
yielding an average site slope of approximately 1.6 percent to the southwest.
Surface soils across the site are classified as SM to SP-SM (silty sands and poorly graded sands with silt), with
cemented caliche horizons at variable depth. Infiltration rates in the caliche zone are low, and no percolation
credit is taken in the hydrologic analysis. The full computed runoff volume is treated as surface flow for the
purposes of this study.
2.2 Existing Drainage Pattern
Under existing conditions, stormwater sheet-flows overland from north-northeast to south-southwest across the
site. There are no defined channels within the property boundaries. At the southwest corner of the site, runoff

--- Page 4 ---
historically discharges toward the downstream regional drainage facility maintained by CCRFCD.
2.3 Offsite Tributary from the North
The site accepts a modest offsite drainage flow entering along the northern boundary of what will become Phase
1. The offsite tributary area upstream of the north boundary consists of approximately 38 acres of low-density
residential and open desert land. Under fully developed offsite conditions consistent with the surrounding land
use plan, the offsite peak inflow at the northern site boundary has been estimated as summarized in Section 3
and Appendix C.
The offsite tributary flow enters the site as sheet flow along the northern boundary and, at build-out, will be
conveyed through the Phase 1 street network to the shared onsite detention basin(s). No offsite bypass channel
is proposed; the accepted offsite flow is passed through the onsite storm drain and routed through detention
along with the onsite runoff.
2.4 Downstream Conveyance
The shared onsite outfall is located at the southwest corner of the property and discharges to the downstream
regional CCRFCD facility via an existing reinforced concrete pipe stub set during earlier regional construction.
The receiving facility has been reviewed against the shared outfall allowance identified in Section 5; downstream
capacity is not the controlling constraint for the site's release rate. The controlling constraint is the outfall
allowance established for Desert Sage Ranch and set forth in this study.
3. HYDROLOGY
3.1 Design Storm
Design storm criteria applied in this study are drawn from the CCRFCD Hydrologic Criteria and Drainage Design
Manual applicable at the time of preparation. The following storms have been evaluated:
• 100-year, 6-hour storm — used for peak discharge estimation and storm drain sizing.
• 100-year, 24-hour storm — used for detention basin sizing (governing storage volume).
Rainfall depths applied are as follows (Enterprise sub-basin, CCRFCD atlas values at time of preparation):

3.2 Method
Rainfall-runoff modeling was performed using CCRFCD-accepted methods appropriate for a subdivision of this
size, applying the Green-Ampt infiltration approach for pervious surfaces and directly-connected impervious

Routing to and through the shared detention basin(s) was performed using the storage-indication method.
Impervious cover assumed at build-out reflects the approved half-acre residential lot type with associated street
and driveway coverage, streetscape landscape strips, and HOA common-area park.
3.3 Tributary Area Breakdown by Phase
The 140-acre site drains as a single system to the shared outfall, but for the purposes of allocating detention
storage the site is subdivided into three phase-based tributary areas that correspond to the phased development

3.4 Peak Discharge Summary — Fully Developed Conditions
Fully developed peak flows to the shared onsite detention basin(s), computed under the 100-year, 6-hour storm
inclusive of the accepted offsite tributary inflow at the northern boundary, are summarized in Appendix C. The
peak inflow at the shared basin(s) governs the storm drain sizing but does not govern the shared outfall release,
which is fixed by the allowance in Section 5.
4. DETENTION SIZING
4.1 Shared Onsite Detention Approach
Desert Sage Ranch is served by a shared onsite detention approach: the detention volume required to attenuate
the site's peak discharge to the accepted outfall release rate is provided in shared onsite detention facilities

--- Page 6 ---
constructed as the subdivision phases advance. Detention basin locations are identified on the phasing exhibit
(Section 6).
The shared approach avoids duplication of small phase-scale basins and consolidates operations and
maintenance for the HOA. Because the phases share the same outfall and downstream facility, the storage
requirement has been determined for the fully developed 140-acre site and then allocated among the three
phases in accordance with the acreage and impervious cover of each phase.
4.2 Governing Design Storm
Storage sizing is governed by the 100-year, 24-hour design storm. The 100-year, 6-hour storm is used to check
peak discharge to the shared basin(s) and storm drain sizing, but does not govern storage. Storage-indication
routing under the 100-year, 24-hour storm, with the outfall released at the allowance identified in Section 5,
produces a total site-wide required storage volume of 16.4 acre-feet.
4.3 Detention Allocation by Phase
Total storage required for the fully developed 140-acre site is allocated to the three phases on the basis of
tributary runoff volume and position in the shared outfall, not by pro-rata acreage. Phase 3 discharges last
and carries the largest attenuation duty; volumes were reviewed and fixed at District acceptance, and are
the fixed planning basis for subsequent phase-level submittals.

The detention allocation established in Table 4-1 has been sized to reflect the tributary area, phase acreage and

5. OUTFALL
5.1 Shared Outfall
The full 140-acre Desert Sage Ranch subdivision discharges to the downstream regional CCRFCD facility
through a single shared outfall located at the southwest corner of the site. The outfall discharges via an existing
reinforced concrete pipe stub previously installed by others as part of regional drainage construction.
Confirmation of downstream capacity has been obtained from the District as part of this study's review.
5.2 Allowance and Cap
An allowance for the full 140 acres at the shared outfall to the downstream regional facility has been established
for Desert Sage Ranch, subject to the following cap:
Q100 ≤ 78 cfs at the shared outfall.
The 78 cfs cap represents the maximum permitted 100-year peak discharge from the fully developed 140-acre
site into the receiving regional facility. Storage-indication routing through the shared onsite detention basin(s) as
sized in Section 4 attenuates the fully developed peak inflow at the basin(s) to a peak release at or below the 78
cfs cap.
5.3 Application to Phase-Level Plans
Because the cap applies to the shared outfall for the full 140-acre site — not to any single phase — phase-level
improvement plan sets are not to compute a phase-specific outfall discharge. Each phase's contribution is
routed into the shared detention system, and the shared outfall discharge remains subject to the 78 cfs cap at
build-out.
6. PHASING EXHIBIT
The Phasing Exhibit, provided as Appendix E and reproduced at reduced scale below, identifies:
• The three phase boundaries — Phase 1 (northern), Phase 2 (central), and Phase 3 (southern) —
comprising the 140-acre site.
• The location of the shared onsite detention basin(s) serving the subdivision.
• The offsite tributary corridor along the northern site boundary.
• The shared outfall at the southwest corner of the site and its connection to the downstream regional
CCRFCD facility.
• The phase-boundary storm drain interconnections that link each phase's contributory area to the shared
detention system.

--- Page 8 ---
The exhibit is drawn at 1"=200′ on a 24×36 sheet; reference should be made to the full-size exhibit in Appendix
E for construction of phase-level improvement plans. Phase-level plans shall reflect the boundaries and basin
locations shown on the exhibit; deviations require formal amendment as set forth in Section 7.
(Phasing Exhibit — see Appendix E.)
7. CONCLUSION
7.1 Summary
This Master Drainage Study establishes the hydrologic and hydraulic basis of design for the 140-acre Desert
Sage Ranch subdivision. The study:
• adopts the 100-year, 6-hour and 100-year, 24-hour design storms in accordance with the CCRFCD
Hydrologic Criteria and Drainage Design Manual applicable at time of preparation;
• delineates tributary areas for the full 140 acres, broken down by the three development phases;
• establishes a shared onsite detention approach with fixed volume allocations by phase — Phase 1 at 4.2
acre-feet, Phase 2 at 5.8 acre-feet, Phase 3 at 6.4 acre-feet, and total site at 16.4 acre-feet;
• confirms an allowance for the full 140 acres at the shared outfall to the downstream regional facility,
capped at Q100 = 78 cfs;
• provides a phasing exhibit identifying phase boundaries, detention basin locations, offsite tributary corridor
and shared outfall.
7.2 Basis for Subsequent Design
Upon CCRFCD acceptance, this Master Drainage Study serves as the master planning document for all
subsequent improvement plan submittals for Desert Sage Ranch, including but not limited to Phase 1, Phase 2
and Phase 3 grading and drainage plan sets and their supporting hydrology, storm drain and detention
worksheets. Phase-level design shall be consistent with the tributary breakdown, detention allocation by phase,
and shared outfall allowance identified herein.
7.3 Amendments
Changes to the accepted detention allocations set forth in Table 4-1, the outfall allowance set forth in Section 5,
or the tributary breakdown and phase boundaries set forth in Sections 3 and 6, require formal amendment to this
study and re-review by the Clark County Regional Flood Control District. Phase-level improvement plans that
propose to depart from the accepted allocations or allowance shall be preceded by an accepted amendment; no
phase-level plan set shall be approved on the basis of a departure that has not been separately submitted to
and accepted by the District.
The CCRFCD acceptance letter dated February 28, 2022 (Appendix F) confirms this requirement and is
incorporated herein by reference.
